cohort: 79 maternal-infant pairs (39 preeclampsia, 40 controls) residing at high altitude (3600-4100 m) in Bolivia.
finding: Preeclampsia, especially when combined with fetal growth restriction, augmented fetal hypoxia and increased maternal and fetal sFlt1 levels, leading to an increased risk of pulmonary hypertension in the neonate but not in later infancy.
